purpose: Test whether the cost of extra inputs, and the failure of all electrodes to beat the best 16, come from training too briefly: the frozen recipe run four times as long, with checkpoints at 1, 2 and 4 times the frozen budget.
claim_boundary: Exploratory for BCI IV 2a, planned after its test results and the input-cost and noise-mechanism results were known. For Lee2019 the predictions are fixed before any of these models is scored on Lee2019 session 2; three predictions, no correction for multiplicity. The frozen 2a configuration (475 epochs) does not change.

L1.claim: Training four times as long shrinks the cost of the 46 noise inputs
L1.contrast: Lee2019 final models, next day: (relevance-16-plus-46 minus relevance-16) at 1,900 epochs minus the same difference at 475 epochs (this study's checkpoints)

L2.claim: Trained four times as long, all 62 electrodes beat the 16 most relevant
L2.contrast: Lee2019 final models, next day, 1,900 epochs: full-62 minus relevance-16

L3.claim: With noise inputs, held-out accuracy of the training day is still rising after epoch 475
L3.contrast: Lee2019 relevance-16-plus-46 fold models (session 1 only): mean held-out accuracy over epochs 1,800-1,900 minus the mean over epochs 425-525
L3.test: interval lower bound above 0 (the plan's 'above 0', read as for L1 and L2)

noise: mibci.noise_mechanism.appended_noise draw 0, the input-cost study's (largest k drawn, cut to k)
analysis: seeds (and folds) averaged within each participant; 95% participant bootstrap (10,000, seed 690); BCI IV 2a on artifact-free session-2 trials, Lee2019 on all; 2a also with the seed error
